additional_concerns: Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preservation of an existing application process into a substantive relief exclusion. That inference is not established by the supplied circular. Preserved processing and substantive disqualification remain distinct possible interpretations.

A pending-at-commencement fact remains historically true after a subsequent decision, withdrawal or resubmission. Using its negation as a permanent eligibility condition may overextend the transition. The circular supplies no rule resolving those later events.
Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question's scope. This avoids deciding their eligibility; it does not establish that legacy applications are legally ineligible.

The explicit commencement date supports the proposed date comparison, but the circular also describes immediate effect. Without the publication date and relevant FAQs, the relationship between those statements and the legally relevant assessment event remains unresolved. An implementation-date test is not expressly supplied.

The introductory reference to home-regulator supervision may describe the measures' purpose rather than impose an independent item (ii) condition. Item (ii) expressly requires home-jurisdiction compliance; importing item (i)'s separate supervision condition is not established.

Actual classifications of applicable home requirements, novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications require evidence beyond these Boolean formulas. The relevant SFC FAQs, applicable home-jurisdiction rules and existing application procedure are not supplied. The two unbound dependency IDs have no identifying descriptions, so no catalogue mapping can be justified.
Notification, filing and post-vetting remain distinct from prior-approval relief. Their omission from these narrowly typed questions does not establish their absence or overall compliance.
